headline: Rhino Rewild Moves 745 Southern White Rhinos Across Africa
meta_description: Rhino Rewild has successfully relocated 745 southern white rhinos across four African countries, with 89 calves born in their new protected homes.
summary_short: A major conservation effort has relocated 745 southern white rhinos to 19 protected areas across Rwanda, the DRC, Uganda, and South Africa, with new populations thriving.
body:
Rhino Rewild has successfully moved 745 southern white rhinos into 19 protected areas spanning Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, and South Africa—a landmark achievement in species recovery.

The scale of the relocation speaks to years of coordinated conservation work. Already, 89 calves have been born within these newly established or reinforced populations, a sign that the rhinos are not only surviving but reproducing in their protected homes. Each new birth represents hope for a species that faced extinction in the not-distant past.

By distributing rhinos across multiple countries and protected areas rather than concentrating them in single locations, conservation teams have built resilience into the populations. Diverse habitats mean greater genetic diversity, stronger resistance to disease, and reduced risk of catastrophic loss. The work of Rhino Rewild and its partners demonstrates that with coordinated effort across borders, species restoration remains possible.
quick_facts: 745 southern white rhinos relocated across four African nations
19 protected areas now home to relocated rhino populations
New populations established or strengthened in Rwanda, DRC, Uganda, South Africa
